evidence_quote: for every instance (L, X, µ) we define a parameter called the zooming dimension, and use it to bound the algorithm's performance

explanation: The cited paper introduces the slow random-walk discourse model and explicitly studies word-pair cooccurrence probabilities, and it compares resulting properties with word2vec and GloVe, supporting the claim that the model matches empirical behaviors under assumptions.
evidence_quote: “The discourse vector c t does a slow random walk ... We are interested in the probabilities that word pairs cooccur near each other...” and “For comparison we also tested these properties for word2vec and GloVe vectors, though they are trained by different objectives.”

explanation: The cited paper presents bounds that scale with the data dimension d, indicating the algorithm’s error/sample complexity depends on dimensionality, which supports the claim that DP-PCA’s sample complexity is dimension-dependent.
evidence_quote: “we expect the second term in Eq. (10) to scale as O(d( log(1/δ)/εn) 1-1/k )”

explanation: The cited paper presents a positive result, showing the existence of a computable learning algorithm for arbitrary computable classifiers (with distribution-dependent sample complexity), rather than proving impossibility of non-uniform learning.
evidence_quote: We have shown that learning arbitrary computable classifiers is possible in the statistical learning paradigm. We first show that there is a computable learning algorithm in our setting.

explanation: The paper itself claims to provide a characterization of proper strong computable PAC learning and to show the existence of PAC-learnable classes that are not even improperly CPAC-learnable, which (by the fundamental theorem) entails finite VC dimension. Thus it reasonably supports both parts of the citing sentence.
evidence_quote: We gave a characterization of proper strong CPAC (SCPAC) learning, that is an effective version of the fundamental theorem of PAC learning; and we confirmed the conjecture that there are decidably representable PAC learnable classes that are not even improperly CPAC learnable.

explanation: The citation is used to reference the APIBench dataset; the Gorilla paper is the source that introduces and describes APIBench, so it is appropriate even though ToolLLaMA’s performance claim is from the citing work.
evidence_quote: We construct, APIBench, a large corpus of APIs with complex and often overlapping functionality...

explanation: The paper introduces a method that uses external large language models to generate class-specific textual descriptors and aggregates similarity across many such descriptors, effectively ensembling fine-grained class representations. This aligns with the claim about DCLIP requiring LLMs for descriptors and converting single-class matching into an ensemble.
evidence_quote: We use vision-language models to visually ground the natural language descriptors generated by the large language models... We can view D(c) as a support set of prototype vectors for class c... we compute the class score s as the mean similarity to support vectors (i.e., descriptor) rather than the similarity to the mean of the support vectors.

explanation: The cited paper specifically studies the modality gap in multi-modal contrastive learning and attributes it to factors including model initialization and the optimization dynamics of contrastive learning, linking it to the cone effect. This matches the claim that recent work found a modality gap and attributed it to the cone effect tied to initialization and contrastive loss.
evidence_quote: “we investigated an interesting phenomenon in multi-modal contrastive learning—modality gap. We analyzed why the gap exists, i.e., the joint effect of model initialization and optimization… For representation learning, prior research in NLP has shown that alleviating the cone effect improves downstream performance. As our work significantly broadens the scope of the cone effect…”

explanation: The citation is used to justify using a BPE tokenization scheme, and the cited paper is the well-known source introducing BPE-based subword units for NMT, making it an appropriate reference for BPE tokenization.
evidence_quote: "best CHRF3 score of 54.1 with BPE-J90k"

explanation: The citation is used to refer to the cleaned-up ReaL labels for the ImageNet validation set, and the cited paper introduces and analyzes these reassessed (ReaL) labels for ImageNet’s validation data.
evidence_quote: In summary, while ReaL labels seem to be of comparable quality to ImageNet ones for fine-grained classes, they have significantly reduced the noise in the rest... Having obtained a new set of candidate labels for the entire validation set...

explanation: The cited paper explicitly analyzes the 100 most highly cited NeurIPS/ICML papers to identify prevalent values in ML research, and discusses “scale” as a salient objective. It is reasonable to cite it to support the claim that scaling up is a sought-after value in influential ML work.
evidence_quote: “Collectively, an interdisciplinary team of researchers analyzed the 100 most highly cited papers from NeurIPS and ICML, from the years 2008, 2009, 2018, and 2019…” … “objectives such as efficiency, scale, and wealth accumulation drive the industry at large”

explanation: The cited paper focuses on GPU-based similarity search methods and states that an implementation is released alongside the paper, aligning with the claim that it describes GPU implementations and that Faiss was open-sourced simultaneously.
evidence_quote: Along with this work, we are publishing a carefully engineered implementation of this paper's algorithms, so that these GPUs can now also be used for efficient similarity search.

explanation: The cited paper analyzes LAION-400M and reports sexually explicit/pornographic content and malignant stereotypes, matching the claim that such problematic content is present in the dataset.
evidence_quote: "in the LAION-400M dataset, words such as 'mom', 'nun', 'sister', 'daughter', 'daddy' and 'mother' appear with high frequency in alt text for sexually explicit content" and "as we have seen from analysing the LAION-400M dataset, the overwhelming visual depiction of certain groups ... is marred with malignant stereotypes."

explanation: The cited paper introduces the CLOC benchmark for online continual geolocalization and specifies it has 39M time-stamped images with natural distribution shifts and 712 classes, matching the citing sentence’s claims.
evidence_quote: “CLOC has a much larger scale: it contains 39 million images taken over 9 years, with 712 classes. Crucially, the distribution shift in CLOC is natural rather than synthetic.”; “We use images with their geolocations and time stamps from YFCC100M.”

explanation: The citation is used as a background pointer to transductive bandits, and the cited work explicitly focuses on transductive linear bandits, aligning with the 'in the spirit of transductive bandits' phrasing.
evidence_quote: Sequential Experimental Design for Transductive Linear Bandits

explanation: The cited paper explicitly frames Fisher information as the sampling analogue of approximate first-order stationarity and develops results within this framework, making it an appropriate source to credit for introducing this notion.
evidence_quote: “we have initiated the study of non-log-concave sampling by proving that … averaged LMC drives the Fisher information w.r.t. the target to zero … We have argued that this is the natural sampling analogue of finding approximate first-order stationary points in non-convex optimization.”

explanation: The cited paper argues an impossibility of strong (universal) robustness and notes robustness may only be achievable under restricted adversaries, aligning with the claim that robustness is feasible only for a well-specified set of attacks rather than all.
evidence_quote: "This only makes the impossibility result stronger." ... "if the adversary is restricted in other ways ... then it may be possible to resist erasure attacks. This is the setting of 'weak watermarking'..."

explanation: The paper proposes using a simple non-parametric nearest neighbor retrieval mechanism as a general-purpose decoder for dense scene understanding, aligning with the claim about Hummingbird.
evidence_quote: we propose a simple non-parametric nearest neighbor retrieval mechanism ... to serve as a general-purpose decoder which we use to evaluate models on semantic segmentation and monocular depth estimation tasks.

explanation: The cited paper does introduce the KD-DTI dataset and reports 12k training and 1k validation samples, but it states 1.1k test samples rather than the claimed 1.3k, so the specific split sizes are not supported.
evidence_quote: Finally, we provide a new dataset, KD-DTI, for discovering DTI from documents... The dataset contains 12k training samples, 1k validation samples, and 1.1k test samples.

explanation: The paper evaluates calibration under dataset shift with comparisons of multiple calibration methods and reports that both accuracy and calibration degrade under shift.
evidence_quote: accuracy certainly degrades as a function of shift for all methods tested ... An important observation is that while calibrating on the validation set leads to well-calibrated predictions on the test set, it does not guarantee calibration on shifted data.

explanation: The cited paper introduces ImageNet-R and explicitly describes it as containing artistic renditions of ImageNet classes, matching the claim about renditions such as art/cartoon-like forms.
evidence_quote: ImageNet-R contains various artistic renditions of object classes from the original ImageNet dataset.

explanation: The citation is used to identify GCG as an existing adversarial attack on aligned LLMs. The cited paper introduces such an attack, so it appropriately anchors the example. The cost comparison is the authors’ own assertion, not necessarily attributed to the cited work.
evidence_quote: Universal and Transferable Adversarial Attacks on Aligned Language Models

explanation: The citation is used to reference a dataset of cable routing robot demonstrations. The cited paper describes a multi-stage cable routing task and explicitly reports collecting a substantial set of teleoperated demonstration trajectories, which reasonably serves as the dataset being referenced.
evidence_quote: collect a total of 1442 demonstration trajectories via a human expert teleoperating the robot at 5Hz

explanation: The cited paper presents OpenFlamingo as an open-source reproduction of Flamingo and explicitly uses Multimodal C4, matching the claim that OpenFlamingo is an initial use-case of mmc4 and an open-source version of Flamingo.
evidence_quote: “we document our experiences building an open-source reproduction of the Flamingo models … The cross-modal module is trained … in our case, two open source datasets: LAION-2B and Multimodal C4.”

explanation: The citation is used to name/identify the BagNet model family (e.g., BagNet-9). The cited paper introduces and analyzes BagNets, including specific variants, so it is an appropriate source to cite when mentioning BagNet-9.
evidence_quote: we investigate how similar the decision-making of BagNets is to highperformance DNNs like VGG-16, ResNet-50...; ...we plot the top-5 accuracy... of BagNet-33

explanation: The citation is used to reference the Word2Vec method for obtaining word embeddings, and this paper by Mikolov et al. is a canonical source introducing the Skip-gram/word2vec approach, making it an appropriate reference.
evidence_quote: Mikolov et al. [8] have already evaluated these word representations on the word analogy task, where the Skip-gram models achieved the best performance...

explanation: The citation is used to point to Word2Vec-style features; the cited paper introduces and describes training word (and phrase) vectors, i.e., word2vec embeddings, making it an appropriate reference for this claim.
evidence_quote: We made the code for training the word and phrase vectors based on the techniques described in this paper available as an open-source project

explanation: The citation is used to justify the concept of a conditional GAN, and the cited paper introduces conditional adversarial nets by conditioning the generator and discriminator on auxiliary information. It need not specifically cover text embeddings; it establishes the cGAN framework.
evidence_quote: Generative adversarial nets can be extended to a conditional model if both the generator and discriminator are conditioned on some extra information y... y could be any kind of auxiliary information, such as class labels or data from other modalities.

explanation: The cited paper introduces a fill-in-the-blank task for comparative questions where an entity mention is masked, matching the description of a dataset of masked coordinated elements with the target being the masked phrase.
evidence_quote: “we introduced the task of predicting masked entity mentions in human-generated comparative questions.”

explanation: The cited paper explicitly describes training a multisensory network to predict whether audio and video are temporally aligned, matching the claim about first training on AV synchrony.
evidence_quote: We train an early-fusion, multisensory network to predict whether video frames and audio are temporally aligned.

explanation: The cited survey explicitly defines a 'tool' in essentially identical terms to the quoted definition, making it an appropriate source for this claim.
evidence_quote: • Tool. For ALMs, a tool is an external module that is typically called using a rule or a special token and whose output is included in the ALM's context.

explanation: The cited paper presents a Bayesian model of pragmatic speaker–listener reasoning in referential communication games, which is the core of the RSA framework and supports using such models to resolve ambiguity via (recursive) Bayesian inference.
evidence_quote: We model human behavior by assuming that a listener can use Bayesian inference to recover a speaker's intended referent... P(r|w, C) = P(w|r, C)P(r) ... [and] assuming that speakers choose words to be informative in context.

explanation: The ALE paper introduced Atari 2600 games as a standardized evaluation platform for reinforcement learning, so it is appropriate to cite it when stating that these games were proposed as a test domain for RL (the exact number 49 pertains to DQN’s subset, not the citation).
evidence_quote: ALE ... transforms each game into a standard reinforcement learning problem by identifying the accumulated score and whether the game has ended.

explanation: The cited paper trains convolutional neural network models on synthetic images of stacked blocks to predict whether a tower is stable, which matches the claim about a deep CNN-based system for predicting block-tower stability from simulated images with simple stack configurations.
evidence_quote: Convnet-based Prediction of Static Stability: We show that standard convnet models, refined on synthetic data, can accurately predict the stability of stacks of blocks.

explanation: The cited paper explicitly introduces the 'Anna Karenina' scenario as the idea that successful models learn similar internal representations and reports providing quantitative evidence for this intuition. This matches the citing sentence’s characterization and rationale for citing the paper.
evidence_quote: "In the 'Anna Karenina' scenario... all successful models end up learning roughly the same internal representations." and "Using model stitching, we are able to provide formal and quantitative evidence... we give evidence for the 'all roads lead to rome' intuition..."

explanation: The MEMIT paper explicitly claims scalability to very large numbers of edits and demonstrates performance up to 10,000 edits, supporting the assertion that it handles many edits effectively.
evidence_quote: Our method scales to much larger sets of edits (100x) than other approaches... Figure 5 plots performance v.s. number of edits on log scale, up to 10,000 facts... MEMIT performs best at large n.

explanation: The cited paper introduces SCE and ACE as calibration measures and describes SCE as extending ECE to consider all class probabilities, aligning with the claim that these metrics measure calibration over all classes rather than only the predicted class.
evidence_quote: "We first introduce Static Calibration Error (SCE), which is a simple extension of Expected Calibration Error to every probability in the multiclass setting."; "Per-class Adaptive Calibration Error (ACE) for a trained 110-layer ResNet on the CIFAR-100 test set."

explanation: The citation is used to introduce/define the “after-kernel.” The cited paper explicitly defines and studies the after kernel as a kernel defined after training, aligning with the description of an empirical NTK extracted post-training.
evidence_quote: A kernel analogous to the FNTK could also be defined after training. In this paper, we call this the after kernel.

explanation: The cited paper introduces and uses the concept of stitching networks via a learned map E to connect layers, matching the description of plugging lower layers from one network into upper layers of another to form a stitched network.
evidence_quote: We test the stitching of any pair of layers in the architecture... reports the accuracy of the stitched network... after learning the map E

explanation: The citation is used to identify the SVD-MV model as the source for initializing weights. The cited paper introduces and names their finetuned multi-view model as SVD-MV, making it an appropriate reference.
evidence_quote: We refer to our finetuned Multi-View model as SVD-MV.

explanation: The cited paper directly investigates the modality gap in multi-modal contrastive learning and attributes its existence to factors including model initialization and optimization, discussing the cone effect. This aligns with the claim that recent work showed a modality gap and linked it to the cone effect arising from initialization and contrastive training.
evidence_quote: In this work, we investigated an interesting phenomenon in multi-modal contrastive learning—modality gap. We analyzed why the gap exists, i.e., the joint effect of model initialization and optimization... prior research in NLP has shown that alleviating the cone effect improves downstream performance. As our work significantly broadens the scope of the cone effect...

explanation: The cited paper studies the modality gap, explicitly manipulates it by shifting embeddings, and reports that increasing the gap can improve downstream performance—matching the citing sentence’s core claim.
evidence_quote: “Modifying the gap by shifting the embeddings can improve different downstream tasks…”; “Interestingly, increasing the modality gap in models like CLIP can improve its downstream performance on several zero-shot learning and fairness tasks.”

explanation: While the paper introduces DomainNet and lists those six domains, it reports notably uneven numbers of images per category across domains, contradicting the claim of an almost equal number.
evidence_quote: The dataset has an average of around 150 images per category for clipart and infograph domain, around 220 per category for painting and sketch domain, and around 510 for real domain... We choose 500 images for each category to form the quickdraw domain.

explanation: The available passages indicate the paper hypothesizes and discusses CNNs exploiting high-frequency components, but do not show that image classifiers achieve high accuracy specifically on high-pass filtered (mostly noisy) images. One retrieved section even focuses on improved recognition on low-frequency images, not high-pass results.
evidence_quote: CNN can exploit the high-frequency image components that are not perceivable to human. ... There seems no apparent reasons why these objects are recognized better in low-frequent images

explanation: The cited paper explicitly introduces a 'list' variant for clustering, analogized to list-decoding, where the algorithm outputs a small list of candidate solutions. This matches the notion of list-decodable learning described in the citing sentence.
evidence_quote: “list clustering: analogous to the notion of list-decoding, the algorithm can produce a small list of clusterings”

explanation: The cited paper argues that all current TTA methods eventually collapse during continual adaptation, not that EATA is an exception. Using it to claim all but EATA degrade misrepresents the paper’s conclusion.
evidence_quote: our work shows that in fact all current TTA methods collapse sooner or later, including methods with explicit built-in anti-collapse strategies.

explanation: The cited paper introduces a 16-class ImageNet subset and explicitly notes it constitutes about one-fifth of the standard training set, matching the claim about using 16 classes representing ~20% of images.
evidence_quote: "We term this dataset '16-class-ImageNet' ... into 16 entrylevel categories"; "This reduced the size of the unperturbed training set to approximately one fifth."

explanation: The cited paper introduces random projection trees and discusses their construction and uses, but the provided passages do not frame RP trees as an alternative to k-means or describe them as producing a distortion-reducing transformation via random projections.
evidence_quote: Both k-d trees and random projection (RP) trees are built by recursive binary splits. They differ only in the nature of the split, which we define in a subroutine ChooseRule.

explanation: The cited paper introduces the HumanEval benchmark with 164 problems requiring generation of Python functions from docstrings, includes function signatures, and defines correctness by passing unit tests.
evidence_quote: “we focus on the task of generating standalone Python functions from docstrings, and evaluate the correctness of code samples automatically through unit tests… we create a dataset of 164 original programming problems with unit tests.” … “Each problem includes a function signature, docstring, body, and several unit tests.”

explanation: The cited paper explicitly assembles an ICLR submissions database (2017–2022) with about 10k papers via OpenReview, making it a reasonable source to cite for using an ICLR 2018–2022 database and its size. The slight year-range and count differences are consistent with using a subset.
evidence_quote: We use the OpenReview ... API to crawl conference data ... in ICLR 2017-2022. We are able to obtain in total 10289 submissions...

explanation: The cited paper is clearly about positional embeddings and input-length extrapolation, but the provided passages do not show that it was the first to demonstrate that absolute position embeddings inhibit length generalization. No evidence here supports the priority claim (“first shown by”).
evidence_quote: Vaswani et al. (2017) discussed two options for embedding positions... They observed similar performance between these two but preferred the sinusoidal approach, which they argued might extrapolate to longer input sequences during inference.

explanation: The paper studies scaling laws in a board game (Hex) and explicitly relates compute, performance, and board size, indicating that for a fixed desired performance the compute scales predictably with board size. This supports the claim that compute required for a desired performance level can be derived from board size.
evidence_quote: Analysed together, the performance of these models reveals a compute frontier... These compute frontiers are exponential in the desired performance, and exponential again in the board size.

explanation: The cited paper establishes correspondences between ImageNet classes and Wikipedia and uses Wikipedia articles to derive features, so citing it for parsing Wikipedia content per ImageNet class is appropriate.
evidence_quote: “ImageNet-Wikipedia correspondences … some of the classes can be mapped to multiple articles.” … “Since ImageNet-Wiki contains auxiliary features … we compute the accuracies of the models using Wikipedia articles…”

explanation: The paper examines geo-diversity in major open image datasets, explicitly including ImageNet and Open Images, and reports amerocentric/eurocentric imbalance, with concrete skew for Open Images.
evidence_quote: "standard open source data sets such as ImageNet or Open Images may not have sufficient geo-diversity..." and for Open Images, "more than 32% of the sample data was US-based and 60%... from... North America and Europe."

explanation: The citation is used to describe the GeoDE dataset as a crowdsourced collection of object images with coverage across six world regions, which aligns with the paper’s scope and dataset description. The rest of the sentence reports the citing authors' findings, not attributed to GeoDE.
evidence_quote: GeoDE (ours) 61,940; balanced across classes and regions Crowd-sourced collection using paid workers; manual annotation Even coverage over six geographical regions (Tab. 3)

explanation: The paper proposes a method for ViTs that performs full self-attention and then, in each transformer block, merges/reduces tokens based on features from attention, progressively lowering the token count across layers—matching the described approach. While the excerpt doesn’t explicitly say “bipartite matching,” it clearly describes per-block token reduction by selecting which tokens to merge after full attention.
evidence_quote: “we apply our token merging step between the attention and MLP branches of each transformer block… use features within attention to decide what to merge” and “In each block of a transformer, we merge tokens to reduce by r per layer… Over the L blocks in the network, we gradually merge rL tokens.”

explanation: The cited work proposes using a sigmoid loss for CLIP-style language-image pretraining (SigLiT/SigLIP) and shows it outperforms the softmax baseline, which reasonably supports the claim that it introduced a pairwise sigmoid loss enabling improved visual encoder capabilities.
evidence_quote: We conducted a study on two language-image pretraining instances that used the sigmoid loss: SigLiT and SigLIP. Our results demonstrate that the sigmoid loss performs better than the softmax baseline...

explanation: The LLaVA paper (Visual Instruction Tuning) indeed connects a CLIP vision encoder to a Vicuna-based LLM and performs visual instruction tuning on curated vision-language data, matching the described integration and training approach.
evidence_quote: “As LLaVA is built upon LLaMA, Vicuna, and CLIP…” and “we consider the pre-trained CLIP visual encoder ViT-L/14… [and] apply a trainable projection matrix… into the word embedding space in the language model.”

explanation: The citation is used to reference LLaVA-Bench as a benchmark; the Visual Instruction Tuning (LLaVA) paper introduces and uses LLaVA-Bench (In-the-Wild) as its evaluation benchmark, making it an appropriate source.
evidence_quote: Table 6: Challenging examples from LLaVA-Bench (In-the-Wild), we provide extremely-detailed annotation for each image for an accurate evaluation.

explanation: The paper uses Wikipedia as a web-scale label space (millions of entities) but the actual benchmark dataset they created (OVEN-Wiki) links only about 20K labels, not 6M entity names. Thus the citation overstates the dataset size.
evidence_quote: we created the OVEN-Wiki dataset, via combining and re-annotating 14 existing ... datasets, and linked over 20K labels to the Wikipedia entities.

explanation: The paper introduces the ARO benchmark to test VLMs’ understanding of relations, attributes, and order, and it frames evaluation around retrieval settings, aligning with an image-to-text retrieval formulation.
evidence_quote: Introducing the Attribution, Relation, and Order benchmark (ARO) for fine-grained evaluation of VLMs' relation, attribution, and order understanding. … Our goal is to understand whether models need order information / compositional understanding to perform well on existing text-image retrieval datasets.

explanation: The DSI paper trains a transformer to predict document identifiers and evaluates different compact docid schemes, including unstructured (atomic) tokens and hierarchical k-means-based structured identifiers, showing advantages such as better scaling—supporting the claim about benefits of learning to decode such codes.
evidence_quote: We also consider unstructured atomic docids, where each document is assigned a unique token, and ... structured semantic docids that describe how to navigate to a document through a hierarchical clustering of the corpus. Structured docids ... scale better to large corpora

explanation: The ReAct paper introduces a framework where agents interleave reasoning (“thought”) with actions step-by-step, making it an appropriate source for instructing agents to generate both a thought and an action at each step.
evidence_quote: REAC T : SYNERGIZING REASONING + AC T ING Consider a general setup of an agent interacting with an environment for task solving.

explanation: The paper reports an empirical finding that CLIP’s effective text length is about 20 tokens and introduces a method that stretches/interpolates positional embeddings to handle longer inputs, aligning with the claim about improving long-text performance.
evidence_quote: “An empirical investigation… reveals that the actual effective length for CLIP is merely 20 tokens.”; “we… keep the first 20 well-trained positional embedding and interpolate the rest… This strategy not only improves the overall length…”

explanation: The cited paper introduces GIT as a generative image-to-text transformer with a text decoder trained via a language modeling objective, and it explicitly mentions auto-regressive prediction, matching the described model type.
evidence_quote: “we present a simple Generative Image-to-text Transformer, named GIT, which consists only of one image encoder and one text decoder. The pre-training task is just to map the input image to the entire associated text description with the language modeling objective.” … “our GIT is fine-tuned to predict the result in an auto-regressive way.”

explanation: The cited paper introduces TIGER as a generative retrieval-based recommendation framework, directly aligning with the claim that it studies generative retrieval in recommender systems.
evidence_quote: We propose TIGER, a novel generative retrieval-based recommendation framework that assigns Semantic IDs to each item...

explanation: The citation is used to point to the source of the MultiArith arithmetic word-problem dataset. Roy & Roth’s paper is the canonical work on general arithmetic word problems and is known for introducing/evaluating datasets like MultiArith, making it an appropriate dataset citation.
evidence_quote: Solving General Arithmetic Word Problems … We evaluate our system on three datasets, each of which comprise a different category of arithmetic word problems.

explanation: The sentence cites the paper as the source of FAB-attack. The cited work introduces the Fast Adaptive Boundary Attack (FAB-attack), so it is appropriate to reference it when listing FAB-attack as part of AutoAttack.
evidence_quote: Minimally distorted Adversarial Examples with a Fast Adaptive Boundary Attack

explanation: The cited paper introduces adding a small number of register tokens appended to the sequence (like a CLS token) and discards them at the end, matching the contrast that it “only appends several register tokens at one end” and does not use them for the final representation.
evidence_quote: We add these tokens after the patch embedding layer, with a learnable value, similarly to the [CLS] token. At the end of the vision transformer, these tokens are discarded... In all our experiments, we kept 4 register tokens.

explanation: The Mamba paper introduces a single-block selective state space architecture with hardware-aware state expansion and a recurrent scan implementation for efficiency, matching the described 'selective SSM block' and efficient recurrent design. While 'competitive to Transformer' isn’t explicitly quoted here, the core technical claims are clearly supported.
evidence_quote: "Selective State Space Model with Hardware-aware State Expansion" ... "Our selection mechanism adds back input-dependent dynamics, which also requires a careful hardware-aware algorithm to only materialize the expanded states..." and "We ... compute the model recurrently with a scan instead of convolution ... The resulting implementation is faster than previous methods..." and "leading to a ... architecture design (Mamba) incorporating selective state spaces."

explanation: The cited paper directly claims that, even with infinite precision, transformers cannot robustly model noncounter-free regular languages, matching the citing sentence’s assertion about theoretical expressiveness.
evidence_quote: We have shown that, even with infinite precision, transformers cannot robustly model noncounter-free regular languages...

explanation: The cited paper explicitly discusses discretizing continuous-time SSMs and specifically mentions using Zero-Order Hold (ZOH) formulas to obtain discrete parameters, which aligns with the claim about deriving a discrete model via ZOH.
evidence_quote: "Discretization... transforms the 'continuous parameters'... to 'discrete parameters'... Various rules can be used such as the zero-order hold (ZOH) defined in equation (4)."

explanation: The cited paper focuses on the Slingshot Mechanism in relation to grokking and reports cyclic phase transitions between stable/unstable regimes and last-layer weight-norm growth/plateau, stating that grokking occurs (almost) exclusively with Slingshots. This matches the citing sentence’s claim.
evidence_quote: "grokking ... almost exclusively happens at the onset of Slingshots, and is absent without it"; "training exhibits a cyclic behaviour between stable and unstable regimes ... the norm of a model's last layer weights ... exhibits a cyclical behavior with distinct, sharp phase transitions that alternate between rapid growth and plateaus"

explanation: The cited paper introduces and names the 'grokking' phenomenon on small algorithmic datasets and documents validation accuracy remaining near chance long after training accuracy is near-perfect before a sharp improvement, matching the described definition and context.
evidence_quote: "Grokking: A dramatic example of generalization far after overfitting on an algorithmic dataset... Training accuracy becomes close to perfect at < 10^3 optimization steps, but it takes close to 10^6 steps for validation accuracy to reach that level"; "On the small algorithmic datasets that we study... validation accuracy starts increasing beyond chance level only after 1000 times more optimization steps than are required for training accuracy to get close to optimal."

explanation: SWE-bench is explicitly introduced as a benchmark built from real GitHub issues and existing repositories, with evaluation via repository test suites, to assess LMs on realistic software engineering tasks.
evidence_quote: we introduce SWE-bench, a benchmark that evaluates LMs in a realistic software engineering setting... models are tasked to resolve issues... The revised codebase is then evaluated using the repository's testing framework.

explanation: The paper clearly introduces task vectors and shows that negation, addition, and task analogies can edit models and improve multi-task performance, but the specific claim that the task vectors are almost orthogonal (preventing interference) is not supported by the provided passages.
evidence_quote: We show that we can edit a variety of models with task arithmetic… For example, negating a vector can be used to remove undesirable behaviors… while adding task vectors leads to better multi-task models… Finally, when tasks form an analogy relationship, task vectors can be combined to improve performance on tasks where data is scarce.

explanation: The cited paper reports cancer bladder cells are more negatively charged at low pH and more positively charged at high pH, which does not support the claim that within normal physiological pH they are more negatively charged; it also does not address nanoparticle attachment.
evidence_quote: Overall, compared to unaffected cells, human bladder cancer cells are more negatively charged at low pH values, and more positively charged at high pH values.

explanation: The cited review specifically discusses the MMP-9 hemopexin domain as a distinct, selective target and argues it can be used to achieve selective inhibition of MMP-9, aligning with the citing sentence’s claim about using PEX-9 to address selectivity.
evidence_quote: The hemopexin domain in MMP9 has a different structure compared to the other MMPs, which means that this domain could be the next interesting target in the discovery of MMP9-selective inhibitors... We will discuss the molecular mechanism of the hemopexin site in MMP9 as the potential protein target...

explanation: The cited paper focuses on tumor cell invasion within a 3D extracellular matrix context, which is topically aligned with a background definition that invasion involves cancer cells moving through and disrupting ECM/basement membrane.
evidence_quote: Our model enabled compartmentalization of tumor and stroma entities... as well as... high-resolution 3D invasion...; ...not designed to examine side-by-side arrangement of different 3D ECM components, which is crucial in understanding the invasion process.

explanation: The cited paper explicitly notes that blending gelatin with calcium phosphate ceramics, alginate, and chitosan improves scaffold mechanical properties, which aligns with the claim that gelatin is often combined to enhance its mechanics and implies its standalone mechanical limitations.
evidence_quote: Gelatin blended with other biomaterials such as calcium phosphate ceramics, alginate and chitosan has improved mechanical properties in scaffolding.

explanation: The cited study on MCF-7 cells reports G2/M cell cycle arrest accompanied by increased expression of GADD45A and p21 (CDKN1A), explicitly linking these genes to the arrest, which supports the association claim.
evidence_quote: IAA treatment initiated G2/M arrest on MCF-7 by the increased expression of BTG2, p21, and GADD45A.

explanation: The cited paper demonstrates using a chemically synthesized N-terminal domain peptide of ANXA1 as the functional receptor/target, which aligns with the claim about focusing on a smaller, functionally relevant terminal fragment to simplify receptor synthesis.
evidence_quote: a chemically-synthesized peptide (MC16) representing the ANXA1 NH2-terminal domain served as receptor for IF7

explanation: The cited paper explicitly states that FTIR is a reliable and sensitive method to identify biomolecules involved in green synthesis of nanoparticles from metal ions, matching the citing sentence.
evidence_quote: FTIR analysis is one of the most reliable and sensitive methods used by researchers to identify the biomolecules involved in the green synthesis of nanoparticles from metal ions [30,31].

explanation: The cited paper reports that interaction between tumor-cell EphB4 and vascular ephrin-B2 promotes angiogenesis and accelerates tumor growth, matching the claim of association with increased angiogenesis and tumor progression.
evidence_quote: “These results suggest that EphB4 plays a role in tumor progression by promoting angiogenesis.” … “These results support a model in which EphB4 promotes tumor growth by stimulating angiogenesis through ephrin-B2.”

explanation: The cited study examined human breast tissues and reports that IFNγ-Rα expression is significantly decreased in infiltrating breast tumors compared to in situ tumors, directly matching the claim.
evidence_quote: A significantly decrease of immunoexpression and of percentage of positive samples (28.9%) were found in infiltrating breast tumors ... Only 41.4% of in situ tumors were positive to α-chain receptor.

explanation: The paper links constitutive/active STAT3 to stem cell-like traits and reports that reducing STAT3 decreases CD44, implying activated STAT3 supports/enriches CD44 expression.
evidence_quote: Since both STAT3 and hTERT transcriptional silencing resulted in the decreased CD44 protein expression ... We reasoned that once STAT3 up-regulated hTERT, hTERT then started to function as an activator for CD44...

explanation: The cited study reports that deleting (i.e., depleting) ERα in a mouse breast cancer model increases metastatic behavior, which aligns with the claim. Although the effect is shown in Ron-overexpressing tumors, it still supports the statement that ERα depletion enhances metastasis in mice.
evidence_quote: Estrogen receptor alpha deletion enhances the metastatic phenotype of Ron overexpressing mammary tumors in mice

explanation: The paper shows that in Myc-overexpressing cells treated with paclitaxel, MAD2 decreases (implying weakened SAC), but it does not indicate melanoma specifically or that paclitaxel-generated polyploid cells intrinsically overexpress c-Myc. It also reports MAD2 increases after paclitaxel in control cells, which contradicts a generalized claim of reduced MAD2 upon paclitaxel.
evidence_quote: “Following PTX treatment MAD2 increased in control cells… indicating that it may be necessary for the PTX-induced activation of the SAC. Conversely, MAD2 decreased significatively in the Myc (+) cells treated with PTX, suggesting that the overexpression of Myc may weaken the mitotic checkpoint.”

explanation: This review focuses on TOPK in cancer, detailing its roles in tumor progression and specifically discussing colon cancer models, making it an appropriate background citation for claims about involvement in cancer progression and relevance to CRC; as a cancer-focused review, it plausibly covers overexpression and clinical correlations.
evidence_quote: “TOPK promotes tumour dissemination... manipulation of TOPK expression in HCT116 colon cancer xenografts is sufficient to influence migration and metastatic growth in mouse liver tissue.” … “Taken together, increased TOPK expression in cancer cells promotes the activation of multiple signalling pathways involved in reinforcing the hallmarks of cancer.”

explanation: The cited paper focuses on ROS/JNK/ATF2 signaling in selenite-treated leukemia cells and does not discuss p53 or its phosphorylation by ATM in the DNA damage response.
evidence_quote: First, selenite induced ROS production and inhibited the phosphorylation of JNK. This inhibition of JNK activation caused dephosphorylation of the transcription factor ATF2.

explanation: The cited paper links Aurora kinases to PKC-induced MMP-9 expression/invasion, not to AURKA overexpression increasing MMP-2, MMP-7, or MMP-10. It focuses on MMP-9 and does not report effects on MMP-2, MMP-7, or MMP-10.
evidence_quote: Aurora kinases are essential for PKC-induced invasion and matrix metalloproteinase-9 expression in MCF-7 breast cancer cells... we found that inhibition of Aurora kinases strongly suppressed TPA-induced MMP-9 expression/secretion.

explanation: The cited paper explicitly claims that DNA methylation-mediated downregulation of ANGPTL4 promotes colorectal cancer metastasis via the ERK pathway, matching the citing sentence.
evidence_quote: DNA methylation mediated down-regulation of ANGPTL4 promotes colorectal cancer metastasis by activating the ERK pathway

explanation: The cited study reports that higher T-cell markers (CD3+ and FoxP3+) are associated with lower recurrence, but it does not clearly support the broader claims about reduced metastasis risk or longer DFS/OS, nor specifically focus on CD4+ or CD8+ T-cell frequencies as stated.
evidence_quote: “high CD3 þ and FoxP3 þ T-cell counts… significantly associated with lower recurrence rate.”

explanation: The paper supports ZNF703 as an immunotherapy target and presents an ERS-related scoring system for CRC prognosis, but it does not demonstrate that the scoring system forecasts prognosis specifically for patients receiving immune checkpoint blockade across diverse cohorts; it only correlates with ICB response predictors.
evidence_quote: “ERSGs scoring system can serve as an effective model to discriminate the outcomes of CRC patients… Patients with low ZNF703 mRNA expression potentially benefit from ICB therapy. Moreover, we identified ZNF703 as a promising target for tumor immunity.”

explanation: The cited paper directly discusses how dysregulation of signaling pathways (often due to mutations) in colorectal cancer leads to unchecked cell cycle progression, escape from apoptosis, and increased invasiveness/metastasis, matching the citing sentence’s claim.
evidence_quote: These dysregulations in the signaling pathways contribute to unchecked cell cycle progression, the increase of cell proliferation, the escape of apoptosis, and enhanced invasiveness and metastasis.

explanation: The cited paper directly studies ESCC and reports epigenetic induction of tumor stemness via an LPS–TET3–HOXB2 signaling axis, which aligns with the claim that LPS promotes tumor behavior by inducing stemness through this pathway.
evidence_quote: Epigenetic induction of tumor stemness via the lipopolysaccharide-TET3-HOXB2 signaling axis in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma

explanation: The cited paper specifically reports that silencing ARID1A and ARID1B structurally disrupts the BAF complex, induces epigenomic reprogramming in neuroblastoma cells, and impairs invasiveness/metastasis. This matches the core claim being cited.
evidence_quote: Structural disruption of the BAF complex, achieved by silencing of its essential subunits ARID1A and ARID1B, exerted an epigenomic reprogramming in neuroblastoma cells ... leading to the impairment of metastatic invasion

explanation: The cited paper directly studies DICER1 impairment in colon/colorectal cancer cells and reports enhanced tumor initiation and metastasis, matching the claim.
evidence_quote: One critical finding of this study is that DICER1-deficient colorectal cancer cells... have an enhanced ability to initiate tumors and metastasis.

explanation: The cited paper reports that hypoxia increases VEGF-A, and that VEGF-A promotes NRF2 nuclear translocation via RAP1B/VEGFR2 with ERK and AKT signaling involvement, matching the mechanistic claim.
evidence_quote: Furthermore, hypoxia promoted the expression of VEGF-A in GC cells... These results revealed that the hypoxia/VEGF-A-Rap1b/VEGFR2 pathway aided in Nrf2 nuclear translocation and that Erk and Akt signaling cascades were also implicated in Nrf2 nuclear translocation.

explanation: The cited paper explicitly describes selecting large genes so that averaging across more probes improves the signal-to-noise of representative gene copy numbers, and it also discusses validating clustering by expecting same-tumor samples to be more similar, aligning with the described reproducibility check.
evidence_quote: we selected large genes because the greater number of corresponding probes resulted in improved signal-to-noise ratio of the representative gene copy numbers. The unsupervised strategy enabled us to set an internal standard to validate clustering results; the copy number profiles in samples of the same tumour should be more similar than any copy number profiles from another tumour

explanation: The cited paper investigates AML and shows GLI1 promotes proliferation via the PI3K/AKT pathway and that this effect is reversed by AKT inhibitors; it also provides evidence of a direct link by showing GLI1 binds a PI3K subunit.
evidence_quote: “the PI3K and AKT inhibitor could reverse the effects of GLI1 overexpression on cell proliferation … suggesting that GLI1 promotes proliferation through the PI3K/AKT pathway.”; “GLI1 increases phosphorylation of essential components of the PI3K/AKT pathway and directly binds PIK3R1.”

explanation: The paper reports that Cx32 downregulation elevates Snail via activation of Wnt/β-catenin signaling and documents nuclear β-catenin accumulation in HCC tissues correlated with reduced Cx32, aligning with the cited claim (with E-cadherin reduction consistent with EMT findings).
evidence_quote: “downregulation of Cx32 upregulates Snail expression and promotes EMT through activation of the Wnt signaling pathway in HCC cells.” “nuclear accumulation of β-catenin in HCC tissues was directly correlated with the reduced Cx32.”

explanation: The cited paper specifically reports that HBx drives aerobic glycolysis via NF-κB p65/HK2, leading to lactate overproduction that activates PI3K/AKT signaling and promotes proliferative (malignant) behavior in hepatocytes/HCC, matching the citing claim.
evidence_quote: HBx initiates the expression and activation of NF-κBp65 in hepatocytes and enhances aerobic glycolysis via the NF-κBp65/ HK2 pathway to overproduce lactate, further increasing hepatocyte proliferation through PI3K/Akt signalling...

explanation: The cited paper reports associations between SCG2 and immune infiltration/macrophage polarization and argues SCG2 plays a regulatory role, rather than stating that how it regulates immune activity is unknown.
evidence_quote: "SCG2 was associated with tumor immune cells infiltration, promoted M2 macrophage polarization... In summary, SCG2 played a critical role in the regulation of tumor immunity"

explanation: The cited paper specifically studies immune evolution from preneoplasia to invasive lung adenocarcinoma and reports downregulation of immune-activation pathways and upregulation of immunosuppressive pathways, including T cell exhaustion and PARP signaling, matching the claim.
evidence_quote: “all three up-regulated pathways in later-stage IPNs … T cell exhaustion signaling, and PARP signaling pathways … could potentially impair immune response.”; “a gradually less effective and more intensively regulated immune response including down-regulation of immuneactivation pathways, up-regulation of immunosuppressive pathways.”

explanation: The cited paper reports that SUSD2 promotes polarization of tumor-associated macrophages to the M2 phenotype and links this to increased angiogenesis, aligning with the claim that SUSD2-driven M2 polarization may increase tumor angiogenesis.
evidence_quote: "SUSD2-expressing BCa cells potentiate angiogenesis... Further, SUSD2 promotes the polarization of TAMs to the M2 phenotype."

explanation: The paper discusses SAMHD1’s role in nucleoside analogue resistance and shows that depleting SAMHD1 increases sensitivity, but it does not indicate that SAMHD1 inhibitors are being developed to sensitize leukemia cells. The only related note is that CNDAC was once suggested to be a SAMHD1 inhibitor, not that inhibitor development efforts are underway.
evidence_quote: “The finding that SAMHD1 levels critically determine AML (and ALL) cell sensitivity to CNDAC is nevertheless somewhat unexpected, as CNDAC had originally been suggested to be a SAMHD1 inhibitor.”

explanation: The review specifically discusses KRAS mutations in lung cancer and notes their common codon positions, and it also states that KRAS is the most commonly mutated RAS family member, making it a reasonable source for this background claim.
evidence_quote: “Mutations predominantly occur at codon 12, occasionally at codon 13, and rarely at codon 61…”; “Overall, mutations have been found in approximately 30% of all human cancers, with [KRAS] as the most commonly mutated family member.”

explanation: The cited paper reports that the EPE peptide reduces viability/growth of several NRAS and NF1 mutant melanomas, matching the claim about inhibited proliferation in a later study.
evidence_quote: “we found that the EPE peptide also reduces the viability of NRAS and some NF1 mutant melanomas”

explanation: The paper does report an invasion-specific melanoma gene signature related to aggressive/metastatic disease, but there is no indication that supervised learning techniques were used to identify it. The methodological detail in the citing sentence is unsupported.
evidence_quote: In addition, many of these invasion-specific signature genes are also upregulated in metastatic melanomas (Figure 3B).

explanation: The cited paper explicitly reports that crizotinib altered the metabolic pattern of A549 cells and inhibited cellular ATP production, matching the citing sentence.
evidence_quote: In conclusion, the present study reported that crizotinib treatment inhibited ... cellular ATP production... Further experiments ... clarified that crizotinib shifted metabolic pattern and suppressed ATP supply...

explanation: The cited paper reports a bioinformatics/omics analysis of metabolic enzyme expression in NSCLC (LUAD) and finds ALDH isoforms upregulated, indicating an association of ALDH with NSCLC.
evidence_quote: A bioinformatics analysis was performed to assess the expression profiles of metabolic enzymes in NSCLC... revealed several ALDH isoforms that were upregulated in LUAD patients.

explanation: The paper reports metabolic signatures in TNBC consistent with increased glutaminolysis, aligning with the claim that TNBCs depend more on glutaminolysis.
evidence_quote: TNBC tumors contain lower levels of Glutamine and higher levels of Glutamate compared to tumors with positive receptor statuses which might result from increased glutaminolysis metabolism.

explanation: The paper directly investigates and shows CXCL12/CXCR4-mediated extravasation of tumor (breast cancer) cells in a rat liver model, which matches the cited clause about their participation in extravasation.
evidence_quote: These findings suggest that CXCL12/ CXCR4-mediated chemotactic extravasation of breast cancer cells is required for metastatic colonization of the liver.

explanation: The cited paper reports that IKKε-driven MMP-3 induction requires PKCα activity and that this induction is mediated via Akt and MEK/ERK signaling, and it links IKKε/MMP-3 to promoting lung metastasis. This aligns with the citing sentence’s claim.
evidence_quote: "IKKε-dependent MMP-3 induction requires PKCα activity" … "PMA-induced MMP-3 upregulation in M27 R/IKKε cells involves both Akt and MEK signaling" … Title: "regulates MMP-3 expression levels and can promote lung metastasis"

explanation: The paper notes that Mint3 is expressed almost ubiquitously, but the provided content does not indicate that some cancer cells express Mint3 at relatively higher levels. Thus, only part of the claim is supported.
evidence_quote: “Mint3 ... activates HIF-1 only in particular types cancer cells and macrophages ... even though it is expressed almost ubiquitously.”

explanation: The paper studies TRAMP tumors and TRAMP-C1 cells, shows hypermethylation of specific CpGs near the Nrf2 promoter, and provides evidence that this methylation suppresses Nrf2 expression, matching the claim.
evidence_quote: “certain CpG sites… were hypermethylated in the TRAMP tumor tissues as well as in tumorigenic TRAMP-C1… cells… Nrf2 expression was suppressed by methylation of certain CpG sites… with… recruitment… to the Nrf2 gene promoter” and “the first 5 CpGs… are hypermethylated in TRAMP prostate tumors and in the tumorigenic TRAMP C1 cells… located adjacent to the previously reported Nrf2 promoter.”

explanation: The cited paper reports that NR4A1 binds the LEF1 promoter and activates its transcription in PTC, with accompanying increases in H3K27ac and decreases in DNA methylation, indicating crosstalk between histone acetylation and DNA demethylation. This mechanistic link supports the claim that NR4A1 upregulates LEF1 in PTC, consistent with downstream growth-related effects.
evidence_quote: “NR4A1-activated LEF1 expression was accompanied by increased H3K27 acetylation (H3K27ac) and reduced CpG methylation (5mC) around the NR4A1-binding site in the LEF1 promoter… The above data suggest that NR4A1 directly binds to the promoter region of LEF1 and transcriptionally upregulates its expression.”

explanation: The cited paper studies curcumin in lung cancer A549 cells and explicitly concludes that curcumin-induced autophagy, even leading to autophagic death, is a potential tumor treatment, matching the citing claim.
evidence_quote: we can only draw conclusions that the promotion of tumor cell autophagy activity induced by curcumin even induced autophagic death is a potential tumor treatment within a limited range.

explanation: The cited paper explicitly proposes a parallel version of the PITC/PIC approximations (pPITC/pPIC) for Gaussian processes, which aligns with a parallel implementation exploiting the PITC-style conditional independence structure.
evidence_quote: The parallel partially independent training conditional (pPITC) approximation... we present pPITC here under the setting of parallel machines and then show how its shortcomings can be overcome by extending it to pPIC.

explanation: The citation is used to support that Random Forests are stable and broadly applicable (or to justify use of the randomForest R library), but the cited work is a reproducibility study comparing implementations, not an authoritative source for RF stability or the randomForest package itself. Its emphasis on variation across implementations even undercuts a stability claim.
evidence_quote: “The reproducibility of random forest models represents a significant challenge due to the variations between different implementations in R and Python.”

explanation: The C2M3 paper explicitly notes that prior pairwise approaches lack cycle consistency and presents a method that optimizes permutations of all layers simultaneously at each step, matching the citing claims.
evidence_quote: "existing pairwise approaches such as [1] do not guarantee cycle consistency of the permutations" ... "optimizes for the permutations of all the layers simultaneously at each step, ... in contrast with other approaches ... which seek the optimal permutations for each layer separately"

explanation: The cited paper identifies imbalance between over- and under-represented samples in KD and proposes re-weighting (via inverse probability weighting) of samples in the logit distillation objective, matching the claim.
evidence_quote: “samples with high propensity are over-represented in the transfer set… the student model would learn less from the under-represented group via distillation.” … “IPW generates a pseudo-population where under-represented samples are assigned with large weights and over-represented samples are assigned with small weights… We further apply IPWD to SSKD as a plugin by weighting the logit distillation objective.”

explanation: The paper does propose a meta-learning energy-based memory model, but the provided text does not indicate that the energy function is the retrieval error or that the model is framed as a generative network. It treats the network’s scalar output as an energy function and trains to minimize reconstruction error, which is not the same claim.
evidence_quote: We propose a novel approach that leverages meta-learning... Our networks output a single scalar value which we treat as an energy function... To ensure that gradient updates (4) are useful for minimization of the reconstruction error (2) we train the combination of retrieval and writing rules end-to-end

explanation: The cited paper focuses on aggregating noisy labels for sentiment in social media, not on inaccuracies of mobile phone geolocations or the completeness/bias of posts, comments, or tags. The claim requires sources about geolocation errors and general UGC bias/completeness, which this paper does not address.
evidence_quote: “our work is applicable to aggregating individual sentiment labels in social media, where users … may express invalid or noisy sentiments to different topics.”

explanation: The cited paper describes removing effects via a GLM and then using SOM to visually analyze the resulting residuals, aligning with the claim of visualizing engine health evolution based on GLM-preprocessed data.
evidence_quote: Section 3.1 describes how the effects of engines and of environmental variables are removed by a General Linear Model, and Section 3.2 shows the visual analysis of the GLM residuals by Self-Organizing Maps.

explanation: The paper introduces the Conditional Latent Tree Model (CLTM) for predicting high-dimensional time series and applies it to educational data by learning a latent tree over knowledge components (KCs) and predicting student learning.
evidence_quote: Here, we introduce a parametric model class, namely the Conditional Latent Tree Models (CLTM), that takes into account the effect of all the above factors for predicting high-dimensional time-series. ... We have two goals for prediction: (1) to learn a latent tree model over the KCs and (2) to predict student learning using KCs as covariates.

explanation: The paper explicitly analyzes the relationship between calibration and their uncertainty wrapper, using NLP test cases, and states that calibration has no direct impact on the wrapper’s outcomes—aligning with the claim that prior calibration does not significantly affect uncertainty estimation.
evidence_quote: “To illustrate the relationship between calibration and the proposed uncertainty wrapper, we take advantage of the simulation of a black-box scenario in the NLP test cases.” … “Next, we validate that the calibration has no direct impact on the outcomes of the wrapper. We use temperature scaling … to evaluate the impact of calibration in the proposed method.”

explanation: The paper does benchmark KNN vs. linear regression for smartphone price prediction, but it does not identify scenarios where each performs better or provide a balanced discussion of limitations; it mainly reports that KNN performs better overall and hypothesizes why linear regression may be weaker.
evidence_quote: In general, the prediction accuracy of the KNN model is higher... This paper hypothesizes that the weak predictive ability of linear regression models may be because some variables do not show a particularly obvious linear relationship.

explanation: The paper does describe ENSO as SST fluctuations and uses an ENSO SST dataset with 1634 weekly points from Jan 3, 1990 to Apr 21, 2021, but it specifies the Niño 3.4 region, not “El Niño region 1.” The region mismatch makes the citation inappropriate for the stated dataset description.
evidence_quote: El Niño-Southern Oscillation (ENSO) is a climate phenomenon... A fluctuation in sea surface temperature (SST) is observed across the equatorial Pacific Ocean... We collect weekly sea surface temperatures from 3rd January, 1990 to 21st April, 2021 in the Niño 3.4 region... to form a set of 1634 data points.

explanation: The cited paper proposes replacing the GRU’s Softmax output with an SVM classifier, matching the claim about introducing SVM as the final layer. While the sentence specifies a linear SVM, the core technique—SVM replacing Softmax in a GRU—is clearly supported.
evidence_quote: We proposed an amendment to the architecture of GRU RNN by using SVM as its final output layer in a binary/non-probabilistic classification task.

explanation: The cited paper is a review on Boltzmann machines and energy-based models, explicitly discussing RBMs/DBMs and defining the probability distribution from an energy function, matching the background claim about EBMs and the Boltzmann distribution.
evidence_quote: We have reviewed basic properties of Boltzmann machines... as well as tractable alternative, namely energy-based models... we have only briefly discussed restricted Boltzmann machines (RBMs)... deep Boltzmann machines... From the energy, the Boltzmann machine defines the probability distribution over binary patterns as follows:

explanation: The sentence uses the citation as a general background statement about what clustering algorithms do. The cited paper is on clustering and explicitly defines clustering as grouping similar objects and separating dissimilar ones, which directly supports the claim.
evidence_quote: Clustering is the task of grouping objects to structures (also called clusters) that maintain internal homogeneity and external separation. Objects in the same cluster should be similar to each other while objects in different clusters should not.

explanation: The cited paper discusses a Bayesian/Hamiltonian-dynamics optimizer and reports faster convergence, but it does not mention MMeLU or MeLU or compare parameter counts. Thus it cannot support the claim that MMeLU requires fewer parameters than MeLU, even if it aligns with the Bayesian convergence part.
evidence_quote: an almost twice faster convergence is ensured using the proposed optimizer... This is mainly due to the Bayesian formulation.

explanation: The cited paper discusses supervised learning and explicitly states that obtaining high-quality labeled data is costly and time-consuming, which applies to multi-class classification as a subset of supervised learning.
evidence_quote: In SL tasks, collecting extensive data with high-quality labels is typically required, while annotating large-scale datasets accurately is costly and time-consuming

explanation: The cited paper introduces FINE, describes performing indirection in function space via trainable weight-basis memories (a fast-weight style mechanism), and is positioned for better out-of-distribution generalization on IQ-like tasks, matching the claim.
evidence_quote: "we present a novel framework named Functional Indirection Neural Estimator (FINE)"; "The weight basis memories allow FINE to perform ... indirection in the function space."; Title: "Functional Indirection Neural Estimator for Better Out-of-distribution Generalization"; "The tasks are similar to popular IQ tasks"

explanation: The cited paper introduces kNN-Per as a personalized method based on local memorization and explicitly describes combining a global (neural) model with a local kNN memory, matching the claim.
evidence_quote: we propose kNN-Per, a personalized FL algorithm based on local memorization. kNN-Per combines a global model trained collectively ... with a kNN model on a client's local datastore. The global model also provides the shared representation used by the local kNN.

explanation: The cited paper introduces a stochastic neural network specifically designed for sufficient dimension reduction and employs probabilistic/statistical machinery (e.g., Markovian structure, stochastic gradient MCMC), aligning with the claim that stochastic neural networks leverage probability and statistics for SDR.
evidence_quote: We propose a new type of stochastic neural network (abbreviated as "StoNet" hereafter) for sufficient dimension reduction... We develop an adaptive stochastic gradient MCMC algorithm for training the StoNet...

explanation: The cited paper uses CGANs and evaluates classification on a credit card dataset, but it does not introduce or 'come up with' Conditional GAN itself. Thus, attributing the invention of CGAN to this paper is inappropriate, even though its application to credit card classification is aligned.
evidence_quote: We used a type of GAN known as Conditional Generative Adversarial Network (CGAN) ... Table 3 illustrates the new classification scores with the subsampled Credit Card data.

explanation: The cited paper describes the LMT algorithm and applies it to meteorological data, not diabetic retinopathy; it does not provide evidence that LMT is effective for DR detection, even if it explains LMT’s combination of trees and logistic regression.
evidence_quote: An application of logistic model tree (LMT) algorithm to ameliorate Prediction accuracy of meteorological data

explanation: The paper does propose deterministic approximate binary gating and uses gradient-based optimization, but it does not discuss minimizing the predictions of a separate targeted network. The claim adds a specific objective (targeted network predictions) not supported by the cited work.
evidence_quote: The second is a deterministic method for model selection by element-wise multiplication of parameters with approximate binary gates… Since the method is differentiable the gates are learned jointly with the model parameters during training by means of empirical risk minimization…

explanation: The paper discusses vulnerabilities such as prefilling and adversarial suffix attacks and notes that deeper safety alignment could improve robustness, but the provided content does not indicate proposals of basic data augmentation as a fix. Citing it specifically for data-augmentation-based defenses against prefilling is not substantiated.
evidence_quote: Remark. ... we show that if we can extend the safety alignment's effect to more deeply suppress the model's harmful outputs, its robustness against all of the three types of inference-stage exploits we list here can be meaningfully improved.

explanation: The cited paper explicitly claims a novel and practical black-box attack setup with limited node access, leverages structural inductive biases of GNNs, and proposes a practical greedy attack method for node classification. This directly matches the citing sentence.
evidence_quote: "We propose a novel setup of black-box attacks for GNNs with a constraint of limited node access, which is by far the most restricted and practical compared to existing work. We demonstrate that the structural inductive biases of GNNs can be exploited as an effective information source of black-box adversarial attacks... [and] propose a practical greedy method of adversarial attacks for node classification tasks."

explanation: The cited paper proposes a Random Search–optimized (enhanced) Random Forest as part of a hybrid method for crop yield prediction, aligning with the claim of introducing an enhanced RF in a hybrid approach for precise agricultural yield estimation.
evidence_quote: “hybrid Random Forest classifier and Random Search approach for crop yield prediction” … “the Random Search algorithm has been used to optimize the Random Forest method's hyper parameters” … “the best outcome… is produced by an improved Random Forest.”

explanation: The paper positions itself as a systematic empirical study of multicalibration in practice and reports extensive experiments across tasks and models to clarify the utility of multicalibration algorithms, aligning with the citing claim.
evidence_quote: “we initiate a systematic empirical study of multicalibration…”; “From the results of our extensive experiments on tabular, vision, and language tasks… we extract a number of observations clarifying the utility of multicalibration algorithms.”

explanation: The paper indeed handles both IMU and video and uses an LSTM forecaster for IMU with thresholded prediction error, but for video it describes predicting the next frame with a CNN-LSTM/parametric model, not a cGAN. Thus the cGAN claim is misattributed.
evidence_quote: “We employ two approaches to detect anomalies with IMU data: … an LSTM based forecaster… predicts the next vector using the previous three IMU vectors… Based on … the prediction error, and a threshold, timestamps are classified as anomalous or not.” “Here, we use a convolutional neural network based sequential model (CNN-LSTM Forecaster) to predict the next frame from the immediate-past frames.”

explanation: The paper indeed proposes a hybrid fuzzy classification method based on dendritic cells and reports improved classification results, aligning with the claim about integrating biological processes for better outcomes.
evidence_quote: "we have developed a new fuzzy hybrid evolutionary algorithm named COID-fuzzy dendritic cell method (COID-FDCM)... Experimental results have demonstrated the effectiveness of our proposed approach by producing more accurate and better classification results"

explanation: The cited paper introduces SapAugment, a sample-adaptive augmentation policy that uses training loss to set augmentation strength, matching the claim of dynamically adapting transformation parameters according to training loss.
evidence_quote: The sample-adaptive policy... takes training loss, l, as input and generates a scalar, λ, that determines the strength of the augmentation.

explanation: The cited paper explicitly characterizes AutoML as automating parts of ML pipeline creation to improve efficiency, including automating hyperparameter optimization, and enabling domain experts to build pipelines with less specialized knowledge—matching the citing sentence’s claims.
evidence_quote: “AutoML aims to improve the current way of building ML applications manually via automation. While ML experts can increase their efficiency by automating tedious tasks like hyperparameter optimization, domain experts can be enabled to build ML pipelines on their own…”; “AutoML aims to reduce and partially automate the necessary manual work… This provides a possible solution for… shortage of professionals with in-depth ML knowledge.”

explanation: The paper analyzes ensemble sampling for linear bandits and provides a regret bound, but the available text does not state an O(√T) Bayesian regret nor that achieving it requires an ensemble size growing at least linearly with T. The specific scaling claim is not supported by the provided evidence.
evidence_quote: We develop the regret bound for ES in Theorem 1 for linear bandits, which approaches the regret bound for TS as the ensemble size increases.

explanation: The cited paper establishes a minimum eigenvalue lower bound (growing as √n) for the design matrix under bandit exploration policies and shows this facilitates both inference and regret minimization, with an explicit application to model selection. This aligns with the claim that data from sublinear-regret (bandit) algorithms organically satisfies such a bound and that it may suffice for model selection.
evidence_quote: We present a minimum eigenvalue bound on the expected design matrix... we show that in action spaces with locally "nice" curvature properties, the above-mentioned minimum eigenvalue grows at the order of √n. We show that this eigenvalue bound enables us to obtain inference and minimize regret simultaneously... We then apply our findings in two practical applications... model selection.

explanation: The cited paper introduces GFlowOut, which uses GFlowNets to learn the posterior distribution over dropout masks in neural networks, matching the claim.
evidence_quote: In this work, we propose GFlowOut, to learn the posterior distribution over dropout masks in a neural network... GFlowOut employs powerful GFlowNets for the variational posterior.

explanation: The cited work specifically proposes using Wasserstein/optimal transport divergences for variational inference, aligning exactly with the claim of a recent paper using Wasserstein’s metric in VI.
evidence_quote: In this paper we introduce the use of optimal transport methods in variational Bayesian inference... Using this family of divergences we introduce the new framework of Wasserstein variational inference.

explanation: The paper proposes a Stein-based variational method on Riemannian manifolds and, like SVGD, it approximates the posterior using particles rather than defining it explicitly.
evidence_quote: "We review SVGD ... [a] particle-based variational inference method. It updates particles ... so that the distribution of the particles ... approaches ... the target distribution." and "our generalization work to Riemann manifold ... [we] solve for the optimal dynamics by a novel method, where the treatment of SVGD fails due to the intrinsically different properties of general Riemann manifold from Euclidean space."

explanation: The paper introduces a GFlowNet-based method for Bayesian structure learning that samples from the posterior over DAGs, shows it can use both observational and interventional data, and empirically compares it to MCMC and variational-inference methods. While the excerpt doesn’t explicitly say “compares favorably,” it clearly reports comparisons against those baselines and presents the method as an effective posterior approximator.
evidence_quote: “We have proposed a new method for Bayesian structure learning, based on a novel class of probabilistic models called GFlowNets… [to] approximate the posterior distribution over DAGs P(G|D).” … “we have already shown that DAG-GFlowNet can approximate the posterior using a mixture of observational and interventional data” … “We compared DAG-GFlowNet against … MCMC … and variational inference.”

explanation: The paper appears to propose a convex relaxation via semidefinite programming, but the provided information does not indicate theoretical guarantees of the form n = Ω(d^2) or numerical phase transitions at n ≈ d^2. Without evidence for these specific guarantees, the citation does not fully support the claim.
evidence_quote: “we first study the usual nonconvex formulation, before deriving convex relaxations based on semi-definite programming.”

explanation: The cited paper frames AUC as a standard, highly favored ROC-based summary for classifier evaluation, which reasonably supports describing it as a gold-standard, threshold-aggregating metric.
evidence_quote: “Over the years, AUC became one of the standard measures employed to assess classifiers' performance... it is widely accepted that AUC should be favored over accuracy” and “A well-known choice, which is typically regarded as the most important statistics derived from ROC curves... is the Area Under the (ROC) Curve (AUC).”

explanation: The cited paper explicitly notes that q (kernel) and C (trade-off) are often chosen via trial-and-error and proposes an automatic method to select them, directly addressing the problem and its solution.
evidence_quote: “q is the kernel parameter, C is the trade-off parameter” … “the kernel parameter and the trade-off parameter are generally selected by some trial and error strategy … Different from these methods, in this paper, we propose to automatically estimate the parameters for SVC in a purely unsupervised manner.”

explanation: The cited paper describes how hierarchical clustering produces a dendrogram that maps similarity and can be cut to choose partitions, aligning with the claim about intuitively determining class divisions via a hierarchical similarity map.
evidence_quote: “a dendrogram displays a general similarity structure of the data by providing a multiresolution view… [and] illustrates how to obtain a partition by cutting a dendrogram at a given height.”

explanation: The paper clearly focuses on minimizing conformal set length at the set-construction stage given a fixed model and conformity score, but the claim that they apply the framework to MCQ is not substantiated by the provided information.
evidence_quote: Our framework operates at the third stage, i.e., we aim at designing the prediction sets assuming a given predictive model as well as a conformity score. ... The missing piece in this picture is length optimization which is the subject of this paper.

explanation: The cited paper proposes using Monte Carlo Tree Search to determine replay schedules in continual learning, which aligns with describing it as an MCTS approach for memory replay.
evidence_quote: We use Monte Carlo tree search (MCTS) to find proper replay schedules... We propose to use MCTS since it has been successful in applications with large action spaces.
